title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the set of notes asks when a group H of conformal and anticonformal automorphisms of a genus-0 conformal surface X ≅ P^1 fixes a compatible round (spherical) metric, and in how many ways. The goal is presumably to make canonical metric choices for the 'surgery' (cutting and gluing) of conformal surfaces.

In modern terms, a compatible spherical metric on P^1 is a maximal compact subgroup of PSL2(C), i.e. a point of hyperbolic 3-space H^3. An H-invariant metric is a fixed point of H acting on H^3.

Previous page, case b): H^+ ≠ 1 is contained in a unique maximal torus T ≅ U(1). T fixes a pair of points {z,z'} on X. One sets N = T·H, an extension of γ = Z/2 by T. The extension class is computed with Tate cohomology:
- if the generator acts trivially on T, H^2(γ,T) = T/T^2 = 0, so the extension splits;
- if it acts by t ↦ t^{-1}, H^2(γ,T) = {±1}/1 = Z/2.
A marginal note corrects which case corresponds to fixing versus exchanging z and z'.

This page, case 1, where N = T ⋊ γ is split:
- The anti-involution σ is not unique. It can be replaced by σ' = εσ, where ε is the element of order 2 of T, so there is an ambiguity of order 2.
- Claim: of the pair {σ, σ'}, one is an inversion (reflection in a circle) and the other an antipodal map.
- Proof, normalizing {z,z'} = {∞,0} so that T = {z ↦ az : |a| = 1}. The antiholomorphic automorphisms of C* are z ↦ a z̄, which fix 0 and ∞, and z ↦ b/z̄, which exchange them.
- Only the second kind commute with T, since b/(\bar u \bar z) = u b/\bar z for |u| = 1.
- For σ(z) = b/z̄ one gets σ²(z) = (b/b̄) z, so σ is involutive iff b ∈ R*.
- The fixed points of σ satisfy z z̄ = b. Hence σ is an inversion if b > 0 and an antipodal map (no fixed points) if b < 0.
- σ'(z) = −b/z̄ has the opposite sign, which proves the claim.
- Choosing b > 0, the inversion σ determines the spherical metric whose great circle is C = {z z̄ = b}, with poles 0 and ∞.
- In H^3 language, this is the point at height √b on the geodesic from 0 to ∞.

Next page: this leads to the 'contradiction', i.e. uniqueness. The antipodal map σ' also preserves C, so σ' and (T, {0,∞}) define the same spherical structure. Case 2 (z ↦ a z̄, |a| = 1, a reflection in the line αR) is then treated.
errors: The previous page's assignment of which N/T action corresponds to fixing versus exchanging z and z' was reversed. Grothendieck caught this himself in the margin ('c'est l'inverse!'). This page is consistent with the corrected version: the anti-involutions commuting with T are exactly those exchanging 0 and ∞.
No mathematical errors on this page. The computations of σ², of the fixed-point set z z̄ = b, and of the sign dichotomy are correct.

ideas.what: Normal form of anticonformal involutions of P^1 commuting with the circle group fixing {0,∞}: z ↦ b/z̄ with b real. b > 0 gives a circle inversion; b < 0 gives an antipodal map.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of anti-holomorphic involutions of P^1 (real structures: P^1_R versus the conic without real points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Möbius/inversive geometry, 19th c.; real forms of P^1)

ideas.what: Twisting by the element of order 2 of T exchanges inversion and antipodal map (σ' = εσ).
ideas.modern_name: The two real forms of P^1 differ by twisting by the central −1, i.e. the Galois cohomology H^1(Gal(C/R), PGL2(C)) has two classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical / Galois cohomology of real forms (Serre et al.)

ideas.what: A compatible spherical metric on the Riemann sphere is determined by an antipodal map, or by a circle inversion together with a pair of conjugate points (poles). An H-invariant metric corresponds to a fixed point of H acting on hyperbolic 3-space.
ideas.modern_name: Round metrics on P^1 ↔ points of H^3 = PSL2(C)/PSU(2); fixed points of compact groups (barycenter / Cartan fixed-point theorem)

ideas.what: Using Tate cohomology H^2(Z/2, U(1)) to decide whether the extension N = T·H splits (previous page, applied here).
ideas.modern_name: Classification of extensions of Z/2 by the circle group

missed.claim: This is an elementary verification inside Grothendieck's unpublished 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' program: whether compact groups of (anti)conformal automorphisms of P^1 admit a unique invariant spherical metric, so that surgery and gluing can be done canonically. The page's mathematics is classical. The only point of record is that Grothendieck worked this out by hand and in Galois-cohomological terms rather than through H^3.
missed.quote: On trouve en fait que {σ,σ'} est formé d'une inversion et d'un antipodisme.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the technical groundwork of the 1983-84 conformal-surgery notes, which are linked to the Esquisse's interest in canonical metric structures on Riemann surfaces. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine classical computation (real forms of P^1, circle inversion versus antipodal map), correct and self-corrected. It is of interest only as part of the unpublished surgery program.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 is probably 'Une fois [choisi/établi] que σ n'est pas unique, il y a une ambiguïté d'ordre 2'. The insertion 'compatibles' sits above it and likely belongs elsewhere ('σ compatible').
'automorph.[?] antiholomorphes[?] de C*' reads as 'les automorphismes antiholomorphes de C*'.
Final line: 'définit une métrique sphérique ayant un grand cercle défini par C = {z ∈ C | z z̄ = b}' (the image shows the curly 'C' / 'E' notation for the great circle).
